test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: State emergency can be imposed in a state if it fails to run constitutionally. Who can declare state emergency?

options.text: The Chief Justice of the High Court

solution:
The correct answer is __**The President of India**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The President of India has the power to declare a state emergency under Article 356 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This can happen if the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Chief Justice of the High Court**

 
 
• The Chief Justice of a High Court does not have the power to declare a state emergency.
 
• Their primary role is to head the judiciary in a particular state and ensure the administration of justice.
 
 
 
• ** The Governor of the state**
 
 
• While the Governor of a state plays a significant role in the state government, they do not have the power to declare a state emergency.
 
• Their role is primarily ceremonial and administrative, and they act on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **The Attorney General of India**
 
 
• The Attorney General of India is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India.
 
• They do not have the power to declare a state emergency.
 
• Their role is to represent the Government of India in legal matters and to give legal advice to the government.
